title: Volume as Base Area Times Height
short: V = B × h: the area of one layer times the number of layers.

blocks.html: You know $V = l imes w imes h$. Grouping the first two factors gives another useful way to see the same formula.
$V = B \times h$, where $B$ is the area of the base and $h$ is the height. The base area is the number of cubes in one layer; the height is the number of layers.

$l \times w$ is the area of the bottom rectangle, and it is also the number of unit cubes that sit on it in one layer. Stacking $h$ such layers gives $B \times h$ cubes. Multiplying in a different order, $(l \times w) \times h = l \times (w \times h)$, gives the same volume, so you can stand the box on any face.

blocks.name: volume
blocks.cap: Each colored layer is the base, $5 \times 3 = 15$ cubes. Four layers: $15 \times 4 = 60$.

blocks.title: Base area given
blocks.q: A prism has a base area of 24 square cm and a height of 5 cm. Find its volume.

blocks.title: Find the height
blocks.q: A box has a volume of 120 cubic inches and a base area of 20 square inches. How tall is it?

blocks.html: Multiplying the base area by another side of the base instead of the height. The base area already uses the length and width; the third factor must be the height, the number of layers. Check: name what each number measures before you multiply.
